# 4 Maccabees Chapter 8 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Seven Brothers Before Antiochus

---

**1** The tyrant's persuasive efforts having been demolished by the noble-minded speech of Eleazar, the guards brought seven brothers before him — handsome, modest, well-bred, and altogether admirable — along with their aged mother.

**2** When Antiochus saw them gathered around their mother, he was impressed and spoke to them:

**3** Young men, I have goodwill toward each of you and I want to extend my friendship to you. I promise you solemnly: if you will give up your ancestral customs and adopt Greek ways, I will make you princes and give you the highest positions in my service.

**4** But if you defy me through stubbornness, you will force me to destroy every last one of you with dreadful tortures.

**5** Have pity on yourselves. Even I, your enemy, feel compassion for your youth and your beauty.

**6** Will you not think this over and turn away from the foolishness of your ancestral religion?

**7** When Antiochus had said this, the eldest brother spoke up on behalf of all of them:

**8** What do you want to ask us? What are you hoping to learn? We are ready to die rather than transgress our ancestral commandments.

**9** We would be disgracing our ancestors if we did not obey the law and let reason guide our lives.

**10** O tyrannical king! Do not think you can overpower the reason in us. We consider ourselves already dead before your tortures even begin.

**11** Your threats do not move us at all. We hold the law to be stronger than any compulsion.

**12** We will never transgress the commands that Moses our father gave us under any circumstances.

**13** And if you torture us for our refusal and then put us to death, O tyrant, remember: you are only giving us a brief suffering.

**14** But you will receive from divine justice the eternal torments of fire for your wickedness.

**15** Are you not ashamed, O powerful man against the powerless, to tear apart the limbs of people who are made of the same flesh as yourself?

**16** Even enemies spare those they have taken captive — but you, our bitterest foe, torture us in our own bodies.

**17** But all this only confirms for us that reason is sovereign over the passions.

**18** For if we were weak and passion-driven, we would give in to you and be led astray. But we have been trained in wisdom and fortified by the law.

**19** Know this, Antiochus: the laws that Moses gave our fathers are our strength, and we will never violate them.

**20** So if you want to torture us for our refusal, go ahead!
